course_name_original: Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales I
course_name_en: Elasticity and Strength of Materials I

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Knowledge and understanding: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, computational and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to plan, design and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems in their specialty, which meet established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate design methods.
Research and innovation: Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Research and innovation: Ability and skill to plan and carry out experimental research, interpret results and draw conclusions in their field of study.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design and research and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, engineering technology and processes and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Judgment formation: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers and people from other disciplines.
Identifies and evaluates the stress situations supported by structural elements.

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for technical competencies
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer, simulation and laboratory practices
Project/PBL assessment (technical capacity, involvement, work done, results, documentation, presentation and technical defense)

assessment_rules: The final learning outcome grade is calculated as 70% of partial grade N1 and 30% of partial grade N2. N1 is composed of 75% from individual written and oral tests (KP1) and 25% from reports (A1). N2 is composed of 75% from individual written and oral tests (KP2) and 25% from reports (A2). If N1 or N2 is less than 5, a resit (R1 or R2 respectively) is required for that partial grade. Resit mechanisms are available for all assessed components.
